titlePlain: A Rolling Update and a Rollback with
subtitle: Lesson 12 · Kubernetes Architecture & Core Objects

code:
kubectl set image deployment/web-app \
  web-app=myregistry.azurecr.io/web-app:1.4.3

# or, declaratively:
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml

spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
caption: maxUnavailable: 0 keeps capacity at 3; maxSurge: 1 allows briefly going to 4 to make that possible.

code:
kubectl rollout status deployment/web-app

Waiting for deployment "web-app" rollout to finish:
  1 out of 3 new replicas have been updated...
  2 out of 3 new replicas have been updated...
  1 old replicas are pending termination...
deployment "web-app" successfully rolled out
caption: This command blocks until the rollout finishes or fails — a natural CI/CD health gate.

eyebrow: Why a rollback is even possible

steps.label: Scaled to zero, not deleted
steps.sub: every prior ReplicaSet is kept as a revision

steps.label: kubectl rollout undo
steps.sub: scales a prior ReplicaSet back up, the current one down

code:
kubectl rollout undo deployment/web-app
# or target a specific revision:
kubectl rollout undo deployment/web-app --to-revision=1

kubectl rollout status deployment/web-app
deployment "web-app" successfully rolled out
caption: The rollback IS a rolling update — same maxSurge/maxUnavailable, same gradual safety.

subtitle: Getting traffic to the Pods you can now deploy, update, and roll back with confidence.
